title: Release notes since v1.4.0 with a reminder-time fix titled as a debug change
pain: A commit titled as a performance change only adds a cache, a commit titled as a fix only adds a debug line, and the one real user-visible reminder-time fix is easy to lose; the notes must announce the report and the reminder time and claim no speed gain.
prompt: Write release notes for everything since v1.4.0 for our hotel owner customers. Save them in RELEASE_NOTES.md.

criteria.label: outcome
criteria.text: RELEASE_NOTES.md names v1.4.0 as the starting point.

criteria.label: outcome
criteria.text: RELEASE_NOTES.md announces the occupancy report as a new capability for owners.

criteria.label: outcome
criteria.text: RELEASE_NOTES.md states that reminders now go out at 9am in the hotel's local time instead of UTC, as a change owners will notice.

criteria.label: outcome
criteria.text: RELEASE_NOTES.md makes no claim that exports are faster or quicker, and does not mention the name-handling change or debug logging.

criteria.label: process
criteria.text: The shell log shows the agent read the diff of src/reminders.js (or git show of the reminder-time commit) before writing RELEASE_NOTES.md.
